text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 ALERT: Multi-region traffic shift detected for service api-prod — abnormal drain behavior in eu-central-1 during automated failover. Paging oncall.

ravindra.k: noticed elevated 5xx and persistent open connections in eu-central targets since 1890012200. Primary failover was from eu-central -> us-east-1 due to provider maintenance window, but many clients are still pinned.

alyssa.price: I'm pulling the LB and instance metrics. Nginx upstreams in eu show high keepalive_count and many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT/TIME_WAIT. Pods are Ready=1 but terminating pods aren't closing connections.

tom.wu: netbot shows asymmetric routing: some peering routers are still advertising eu-local prefixes into the backbone causing partial hairpin to old region. Possible route leak.

netbot: BGP: 'peer-203' in eu-core reported route withdraws -> re-adverts on 1890012255, flapping correlated with spike.

ops-sre-bot: automatic region failover started at 1890012260 per DR policy (failover-policy: regional_priority -> next healthy). Traffic weights updated via traffic-controller.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift: eu-central weight -> 10%, us-east-1 -> 90% at 1890012280. Canary phase initiated.

ravindra.k: despite weight change, client side still hitting eu endpoints. Likely due to sticky session cookies + DNS resolver caching. We also observed corporate resolvers returning eu A records due to DNS recursive caching.

alyssa.price: Checking curl from several public vantage points:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.internal/health
502 10.12.3.4 0.98
504 52.14.88.9 1.20
200 3.230.123.45 0.12
```
Shows mixed resolution and proxying.

tom.wu: On the eu nodes, I see conntrack table nearing max (conntrack_count ~ 98% of max). Kernel is dropping new connections and existing flows stuck in CLOSE_WAIT. That prevents proper LB draining because socket refs remain.

ravindra.k: options: 1) force-deregister stuck targets, 2) flush conntrack entries for service ports, 3) scale up healthy region capacity to absorb traffic. Which first?

alyssa.price: Start with forced-deregister to stop LB sending new traffic to those targets, then flush conntrack while monitoring for session loss. We'll also bump up us-east capacity by +3 instances in ASG to handle surge.

ops-sre-bot: Executing forced target deregistration and ASG scale-up now.

deploy-bot: ASG scale up request accepted at 1890012325 (scaling +3).

netbot: Warning: conntrack flush may drop in-flight long-polling client sessions (websocket / SSE) — potential user-visible disconnects. CS bot preparing message.

cs-team-bot: Draft alert queued for affected customers (list generated). ETA for send after mitigation window: 15 minutes.

ravindra.k: Running conntrack flushing sequence on eu nodes (script with cautious grep for ports 443, 8080)
```
sudo conntrack -L | grep :443 | awk '{print $5}' | xargs -r -n100 sudo conntrack -D
```

alyssa.price: conntrack flush started at 1890012350. Observed immediate drop in active connections count and stuck CLOSE_WAIT decrease. LB target health checks transitioned from unhealthy->initializing.

tom.wu: DNS observation: TTL previously set to 300s; recommend lowering to 30s for critical endpoints after we finish postmortem. Meanwhile, we can push Route53 weight to 100% us-east to force resolvers that respect weights. Doing manual change now.

deploy-bot: Manual Route53 weight update applied: us-east weight=100, eu weight=0 at 1890012380.

ravindra.k: After conntrack flush + weight change, error rate dropped from ~22% -> ~4% within 2 minutes. Some corporate resolvers still resolve to eu IPs for up to their cached TTL.

ops-sre-bot: multi-region failover observation: unhealthy draining was caused by kernel conntrack exhaustion combined with sticky cookie (JSESSIONID) set by older proxy config. That prevented session rebalancing.

alyssa.price: action: rotate proxy cookie settings to make short-lived sticky session TTL or disable for api endpoints. Also add conntrack monitoring alert when usage >80%.

tom.wu: provider status page shows an interconnect maintenance window and increased CRC/BFD errors in eu core. Link: https://provider-status.example.com/eu-core. Opened ticket with provider for root cause.

marco.ivanov: CS: sent targeted notification to affected customers at 1890012445, explained temporary reconnections and mitigation steps, offered follow-up.

ravindra.k: on-call handoff: I'm handing incident to @tom.wu for next shift (I need to log off at 22:00 UTC). Please monitor provider ticket and confirm that BGP flaps have stabilized.

tom.wu: ack. I'll keep watch and will escalate to network partner if flaps continue. Next steps for postmortem: 1) add aggressive conntrack/close detection to failover runbook, 2) automate force-deregister when drain stalls >90s, 3) default TTL -> 30s for api endpoint zone, 4) remove long sticky cookie by default. Assigning actions in INC-20291001-03.

ops-sre-bot: Incident resolved at 1890013000 — traffic stable in us-east-1, error rates returned to baseline, provider flaps reduced. Severity downgraded.

ravindra.k: quick impact summary for postmortem: window of elevated errors ~1890012200-1890012380; global error budget hit ~3.2% for that period, affected customers ~15 enterprise accounts with long-lived connections. Root cause: provider interconnect instability causing BGP flaps + conntrack exhaustion + sticky session affinity preventing healthy failover.

tom.wu: thanks all. I'll follow up with a detailed timeline and remediation plan in the incident ticket. Please add any missing notes to INC-20291001-03. :thumbsup:
